snip.t: Serum methylmalonic acid and homocysteine\nlevels—​these are elevated in vitamin B​12​ deficiency\nand are useful if the vitamin B​12​ level is borderline.
Serum vitamin B12 levels are low, and the serum concentrations of methylmalonic acid and homocysteine are usually elevated.
In untreated patients, methylmalonic acid and total homocysteine levels are often helpful because they are greatly elevated in the majority of those with clinical signs of B12 deficiency.
His serum vitamin B12 and methylmalonic acid assays are normal.
Without B12, homocysteine and methylmalonic acid both rise.
